summary: Thomas Hand, father of Emily Hand, tells Fox News Digital his daughter will turn nine on Nov. 17 in the tunnels of Gaza, where she was taken hostage by Hamas from kibbutz Be'eri on Oct. 7. Billboards of Israeli hostages will go up in Times Square, Madison Square Garden and many other US locations to keep attention on the captives. Hand describes his grief, his earlier belief she was dead, and the distress of watching a woman tear down hostage posters in Manhattan.
one_line: On her ninth birthday, Emily Hand is held hostage in Gaza, as her father Thomas Hand describes his anguish and billboards highlight the hostages across the US.
key_facts: Emily Hand turns nine on Friday, Nov. 17, 2023, while held hostage in Gaza; she loves dancing and Beyoncé songs.
Emily was taken by Hamas terrorists on Oct. 7 from a sleepover at a friend's house in kibbutz Be'eri, along with her friend Hila and Hila's mother Raya.
Emily's mother died of breast cancer when Emily was 2½ years old; she has been raised by her father Thomas Hand and the kibbutz community.
Thomas Hand was first told his daughter was dead, then learned she had been taken hostage; an eyewitness saw her led away, and officials found no blood matching her DNA in the bomb shelter or house.
Hand was born in Dublin, Ireland, raised Roman Catholic, is not Jewish, and moved to Israel in 1992.
Billboards of hostages go on display at 8 a.m. Friday in Times Square and Madison Square Garden, plus 1,500 other locations in 48 US cities, organized by Bring Them Home Now.
About 240 Israeli civilians were taken hostage on Oct. 7; the youngest was 9 months old.
Hand has lost about 8 kilos (18 pounds) since the abduction, eats little and has trouble sleeping.
Be'eri lost 112 people murdered out of a population of about 1,200, and its residents now live in hotels across Israel as refugees.
Be'eri resident Yehudit Weiss, a hostage, was found dead by the IDF in a building adjacent to Al-Shifa Hospital in Gaza.
After the interview at Central Synagogue in Manhattan, a woman tore down hostage posters while Hand and Michael Levy watched, and Hand shouted angrily.
Hand says Emily "doesn't know if I was killed or kidnapped" and is "in terror every day."
